text.p: Following are the main stories in Friday's Malaysian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- ALL newspapers lead with the sacking of a woman deputy minister and a woman senator in a case involving the transfer of 1.8 million ringgit (about $715,000) in funds belonging to the Women's Wing of Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad's party UMNO.

-- The Anti-Corruption Agency has proposed that the fine for corruption offences be increased to between 50,000 and 100,000 ringgit (about $20,000 to $40,000), said director-general Shafee Yahaya. Offenders are currently fined up to 10,000 ringgit or jailed up to five years.
-- Fifty-five members of opposition Islamic party PAS will be charged in court for demonstrating against the presence of an Israeli cricket team in Malaysia on April 4.
-- The Malaysian Cabinet has approved heavier penalties sought by the Anti-Corruption Agency against those found guilty of graft.
-- Prime Minister Mahathir Muhammad ordered his party UMNO to wage an all-out war against corruption in the party. He was speaking in a conference call from London to supreme council members of UMNO.
